Why Australians are re-shopping for cleaners in 2026

Oneflare — for years one of Australia's biggest home-services marketplaces — was retired by its owner Airtasker on 30 June 2026, and every Oneflare address now redirects to Airtasker. That left hipages (whose tradie plans run A$139–A$649 per month, before GST, on contract terms) and Airtasker as the main options for finding a cleaner.

Plenty of households and cleaning businesses are looking for a simpler path: know a fair price first, write one good request, and send it directly. That is exactly what this page does. Sources: Oneflare closure & hipages plan pricing, Bark Australia cleaning cost guide.

Cleaning services & what they usually cost

Eight kinds of clean, eight different jobs. Each section covers what the service involves, what Australians typically pay in 2026, and a shortcut that pre-fills the estimator for you.

Regular house cleaning — weekly & fortnightly

Typically A$120–A$220 per visit · A$35–A$60/hr

The maintenance clean that keeps a lived-in home under control. Weekly suits busy families and pet owners; fortnightly is the most popular rhythm for couples and smaller households. Recurring bookings usually run 5–15% cheaper per visit than one-offs because the home never gets far behind.

  • Kitchen benches, stovetop, splashback & sink
  • Bathrooms: shower, bath, toilet, mirrors, vanity
  • Dusting, vacuuming and mopping throughout
  • Bins emptied; beds made on request

Deep cleaning

Typically A$300–A$600 for a standard home

A one-off, top-to-bottom reset for homes that have slipped — or the smart first step before starting a regular service. Deep cleans take roughly twice as long as a maintenance visit and tackle the build-up regular cleans skip. Ideal before guests, after renovations, or when moving into a home someone else lived in.

  • Everything in a regular clean, plus:
  • Grout, tiles and shower screens scrubbed
  • Skirting boards, doors, light fittings & fans
  • Rangehood, splashback grease and appliance exteriors

End of lease cleaning (bond cleaning)

Typically A$350–A$550 (2-bed unit) · A$550–A$900+ (3–4 bed house)

The full vacate clean your real estate agent inspects against the condition report. It is the most checklist-driven clean there is — oven, walls, windows, tracks, blinds and often carpet steam cleaning are all in scope. Get the agent's own checklist and hand it to your cleaner; a written re-clean promise (if cleaning items are flagged within the stated window) is worth asking for, but no cleaner can guarantee your bond — that decision belongs to the property manager.

  • Full kitchen including inside oven & rangehood
  • Walls spot-cleaned, skirting, doors & tracks
  • Windows inside (outside where safely reachable)
  • Carpet steam cleaning usually quoted as an add-on

Spring cleaning

Typically A$280–A$550 for a standard home

The seasonal deep-dive: once or twice a year, usually September–November or before the Christmas hosting season. Very similar in scope to a deep clean, with extra attention to the jobs that only come around annually — high dusting, ceiling cobwebs, exhaust fans, and sorting out the laundry and pantry zones.

  • Deep-clean scope across the whole home
  • Cobweb removal, fans & exhaust covers
  • Inside cupboards and pantry wipe-down (on request)
  • Pairs well with oven and window add-ons

Oven cleaning

Estimator range A$120–A$220 depending on home size & oven condition

The job everyone puts off. A dedicated oven clean strips racks and trays, degreases the cavity, glass and seals, and usually covers the cooktop and rangehood filters too. It's a standard line item in end of lease checklists and the single most common add-on to deep and spring cleans.

  • Racks, trays and glass door detailed
  • Cavity degreased; seals and knobs wiped
  • Cooktop and rangehood filters included by most cleaners
  • Double ovens and wide stoves cost more — say so in your request

Carpet & steam cleaning

Estimator prices per room, whole home from ~A$150

Hot water extraction (steam) cleaning lifts the grit vacuuming can't reach and is routinely required by lease agreements at vacate time — keep the receipt for your agent. Also worth booking for allergy management, pet accidents and pre-baby cleans. Upholstery and rug cleaning are usually quoted alongside.

  • Per-room pricing; stairs and hallways extra
  • Pre-treatment of high-traffic areas and spots
  • Vacate cleans: ask for a tax invoice/receipt for your agent
  • Drying time typically 4–6 hours with airflow

Window cleaning

Estimator range based on home size, inside & out

Glass, frames, tracks and flyscreens — the finishing touch that makes a deep or spring clean actually look finished. Two-storey homes cost more because of ladder and pole work, and exterior-only services are common in coastal suburbs where salt spray builds up fast.

  • Interior and/or exterior glass
  • Tracks vacuumed and wiped (a bond-clean must)
  • Flyscreens brushed or washed
  • Tell your cleaner if any glass is tinted or leadlight

Apartment cleaning

Typically A$100–A$180 per regular visit

Units, apartments and townhouses clean faster than houses — but building rules matter. Strata buildings often restrict cleaner access hours, require lift bookings for equipment, and have visitor parking limits. A good quote request mentions your floor, lift access and parking so the cleaner's price is right the first time. Short-stay and Airbnb units need turnover-style cleans with linen change — list that under extras.

  • Compact-space regular or deep cleans
  • Balcony sweep and glass balustrade wipe
  • Linen change available as an extra
  • Note lift access & parking in your request

NT

The city, Palmerston and the northern suburbs around Casuarina and Nightcliff — wet-season mould and dust make deep cleans a dry-season ritual.

TAS

Hobart

House cleaning questions, answered

The things Australians ask most before booking a cleaner in 2026.

How much does a house cleaner cost in Australia in 2026?

Most cleaners charge between A$35 and A$60 per hour, and a standard regular clean of a typical home usually lands between A$120 and A$220 per visit. Where you sit in the range depends on bedrooms and bathrooms, your city, and the state of the home. The estimator at the top of this page applies that same rate card to your details.

How much does end of lease (bond) cleaning cost?

A 2-bedroom unit typically falls in the A$350–A$550 range; a 3–4 bedroom house commonly runs A$550–A$900 or more once oven, walls, windows and carpet steam cleaning are included. Always confirm exactly what is included against your agent's own checklist before booking — that checklist, not advertising, defines the job.

What's the difference between a regular clean and a deep clean?

A regular clean maintains a home that's already in reasonable shape: kitchen surfaces, bathrooms, floors, dusting and bins. A deep clean is a longer top-to-bottom service that adds grout and tile scrubbing, skirting boards, rangehoods, light fittings and built-up grime. Most households book a deep clean first, then switch to regular weekly or fortnightly visits to hold the standard.

Do cleaners bring their own products and equipment?

Most professional cleaners bring their own products, vacuum and mop. Some independent cleaners ask you to supply a vacuum or specific products — especially if you prefer eco or allergy-friendly options. Say what you'd prefer in your quote pack notes so the price you get back assumes the right setup.

Will a bond clean guarantee I get my full bond back?

No. The final decision sits with your property manager and the entry condition report, and bond can be held for things cleaning can't fix — damage, rent arrears, garden condition. Many end of lease cleaners do offer a re-clean promise if the agent flags cleaning items within a set number of days; ask for it in writing before you book.

Is weekly or fortnightly cleaning cheaper per visit?

Usually, yes. Recurring bookings commonly attract roughly 5–15% off the one-off price per visit, with weekly discounted more than fortnightly — the home stays in better shape, so each visit takes less time. If budget is tight, fortnightly with a monthly “extra hour” for rotating jobs (oven, windows, fridge) is a popular middle path.

How does the quote pack on this site work?

You enter your suburb, home size and cleaning type, and the estimator shows an instant price range based on current Australian market rates. Add your contact details and the page builds a tidy quote request summary right here in your browser. Nothing is sent anywhere automatically — you copy or download the pack and send it to whichever local cleaners you choose, however you like.

Are the cleaners here vetted, verified or exclusive?

No — and be wary of any site that implies otherwise without showing its checks. This site does not employ, vet, rank or endorse cleaners, and it isn't a booking platform. It's a pricing and quote-preparation tool. Always check a cleaner's ABN, reviews, insurance, and a police check for anyone who'll hold a key to your home.

Do I need to be home during the clean?

Most people aren't, after the first visit or two. Common arrangements are a lockbox, garage code, or a key held by the cleaner. Whatever you choose, spell it out in the access field of your quote pack, and agree on how the home is locked up afterwards.
